subject: Pilot extension: top-up credits vs capacity burst — proposal request
messages:
From: Julia Smith <julia.smith@evohealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot extension options — credits vs fixed burst

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the onboarding walkthrough last week — the team has been impressed with throughput and latency so far. We have a couple of asks as we reach week 5 of the 6-week pilot:

1) We expect a spike in inference volume over the next 2 weeks as we run a larger internal validation cohort.
2) We want to avoid unexpected overage charges but also would like a predictable way to extend the pilot for two additional weeks.

Can you outline options for: (A) a top-up credit we can purchase to cover the extra 2-weeks, (B) a temporary SKU-based burst capacity with a clear cap, or (C) a short committed tier with a limited discount? Our procurement team prefers option A, but they want the math (credits vs estimated calls) and an addendum to the current SOW.

Attached is our current_usage_snapshot.csv — it shows token usage and peak concurrent requests for the last 7 days.

Also, do you have a standard contract addendum or a quick mutual action plan we can sign to get the extension in place before the pilot ends?

Thanks — Julia
Julia Smith
Head of ML Ops
EvoHealth

Attachment: current_usage_snapshot.csv (CSV, 28KB)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Smith <julia.smith@evohealth.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Apr 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot extension options — credits vs fixed burst

Hi Julia — appreciate the usage file, that helped. Two quick proposals below (numbers illustrative, we can tighten after a quick sync):

Option 1 — Time-boxed credit top-up (fastest to implement)
- 2-week top-up: $12,000 in consumption credits applied to the pilot project
- Covers ~estimated 55M tokens based on your supplied snapshot and projected spike
- No contract change required beyond a one-page addendum (we can DocuSign)

Option 2 — SKU burst (capped throughput)
- Reserve temporary burst SKU for 2 weeks: 200 r/s backing pool, billed as a fixed overlay of $9,000 plus metered overage at standard rates
- Includes an explicit concurrency cap and a guaranteed SLO for peak latency during the burst window

Option 3 — Short committed tier (2-week min)
- Commit to a small reserved capacity for 2 weeks at a 15% discount vs hosted overage rate; converts to consumption credits if you convert to Dedicated within 60 days

Recommended path: Option 1 for speed (procurement can approve credits quickly), plus a short addendum that we countersign. I’ve attached a draft SOW addendum (SOW_draft_v2.pdf) and a suggested mutual action plan link.

If helpful, Rafael can propose a hybrid that combines a smaller top-up + capped SKU burst; that reduces both procurement friction and operational risk. Can we do a 20-minute call tomorrow to pick one?

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0192

Attachment: SOW_draft_v2.pdf (PDF, 46KB)
Related: https://docs.redwood.com/sales/mutual-action-plan/EVO-421

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Julia Smith <julia.smith@evohealth.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot extension options — credits vs fixed burst

Monica / Julia — looping in a slightly different structure we’ve used successfully for similar customers:

Hybrid top-up + milestone credit
- Immediate 2-week top-up: $8,000 consumption credit (applied to pilot) to cover projected burst
- Milestone: if EvoHealth commits to a 3-month Dedicated reservation within 45 days, Redwood converts an additional $6,000 into a credit that applies against the first month of Dedicated usage
- If EvoHealth does not convert, the milestone credit does not apply (no refund)

Why this works:
- Procurement more comfortable with a smaller near-term spend (the $8k)
- Commercial team protects conversion economics with the milestone credit
- Ops gets a predictable cap during the extension window (we’ll stand up a temporary burst pool)

Approval note: For the milestone to be valid we need approval from Sales Leadership to grant the $6k conversion credit; Monica, can you confirm if you have sign-off or if I should route?

I’ve also added a short HubSpot note for the ECO-POC timeline: https://hubspot.redwood/deals/EVO-POC-421 — feel free to comment.

Rafael Mendes
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai | (650) 555-0210

From: Julia Smith <julia.smith@evohealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 02 May 2026 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot extension options — credits vs fixed burst

Monica / Rafael — thanks for the clear options and the hybrid suggestion. Procurement reviewed and we can move forward on a compromise that minimizes internal approvals:

Agreed terms for 2-week extension (pilot):
- Immediate consumption credit: $12,000 applied to pilot project (covers estimated usage per the CSV).
- Overflow burst: if we exceed credits, overflow will be routed to a temporary burst SKU at 50% off the hosted overage rate for the extension period only. Cap on burst spend for the window: $6,000.
- Milestone conversion: EvoHealth has an option to convert $4,000 of the initial credit to apply to the first month of Dedicated if we execute a Dedicated reservation within 45 days.

Please prepare a one-page addendum + DocuSign and I’ll route for signature. I’ve attached a signed MOU stub to expedite countersignature.

Best,
Julia Smith
Head of ML Ops | EvoHealth
julia.smith@evohealth.com

Attachment: mou_evohealth_signed.pdf (PDF, 12KB)
